name: shell-plugins-fec9cd00-blind28-ots
instr:
# 1Password shell extensions: importers, self-checks and helpers misbehaving, diagnosed without a test suite

Sweeping a machine for secrets that other command-line tools have already saved there has become badly unreliable, and the trouble is confined neither to one service nor to one kind of file; several unrelated helpers now answer simple questions wrongly as well. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

The sweep turns up nothing at all for a long list of services whose secrets are plainly sitting on disk, while for those same services reading the secret out of the environment keeps working exactly as before. A YAML settings file recording a public identifier, a matching secret, a default region, a default zone, a project identifier and an organisation identifier offers no candidate. A JSON file kept beneath a shared settings-store directory holding an e-mail address, a long key and a project subdomain offers none. A JSON file holding several named profiles, each with an account identifier, a key and a secret, offers neither of the two it used to. A JSON file at its tool's default location holding one long signed token offers none, and neither does a JSON file in the home directory that stores a single named key together with its display name. A settings file listing contexts and servers offers nothing even for the context that carries both a server address and a token.
